title: Strong evidence: divergent but full-length rpoB orthologue
why: Independent truth is POSITIVE and all three Genome Skeptic arms detect rpoB. The conventional nucleotide-identity baseline misses it because a fixed 80% identity / 80% coverage rule does not fit a divergent orthologue. The family HMM and multi-member protein search carry the call.

title: Unresolvable truth: rpoB in a reduced Wolbachia genome
why: Independent adjudicators could not resolve truth (best reference similarity 0.475), so the case is excluded from accuracy. Genome Skeptic and the RefSeq/PGAP comparator disagree. The case shows why 19 of 60 M60 cases were reported separately rather than forced into a correct/incorrect label.

title: Verification overrides a homology hit, and is wrong
why: The conventional baseline reported tetA (identity and coverage at least 80%). All three Genome Skeptic arms returned 'not detected'; independent truth is POSITIVE. Post-hoc analysis attributed the shared tetA errors to frozen family-state rules (refine_weak_family_classification relabels the competitive result as ambiguous_family, which the validator treats as a hard negative). A one-iteration counterfactual patch recovered this case; the repaired adjudicator was frozen as V5 after M60. It is shown because skepticism can also cause errors.

title: Critic challenges the planner and requests a second test
why: This is the only M60 case in which the critic did not accept the planner's plan and triggered a second registered measurement. The final endpoint still came from the deterministic validator and matched GS-Deterministic, as in all 60 cases.
